changes: - **Legend parsing fix (main false-alarm source).** List-style legends ("***, **, and * … 1%, 5%, and 10%") are now parsed first, so `*` is no longer mapped to 1%.

hypothesis: Every reported inferential quantity implies the others: estimate ÷ SE gives a z/t, which gives a p-value, which gives a significance marker under the table's own star legend. changes: - **Fixed the legend-parser bug behind the star_flip recall drop.** The list-style regex could split a single "***" into several tokens, which produced a partial legend and silently disabled most star checks. Symbol runs are now matched whole, and at least two distinct symbols are required.

changes: Added a cross-occurrence check for the remaining sign_flip misses, which occur in SE-only tables where no single cell reveals the error. When an identical |estimate|/(SE or t) pair appears more than once in the paper, such as a baseline coefficient repeated in robustness or mechanism tables, the minority sign is flagged. Differing significance markers are also flagged, but only when the occurrences share the same star legend. Everything else is unchanged from version 6.

changes: No functional change from version 9; I am resubmitting it as the final consolidated module. On the visible dev set it ties version 5's best score (0.4119), with the same recall and the same single false-alarm paper. It adds the generalising sub-checks: text statistic → p, CI order, CI width vs SE, column-calibrated CI centring, and level-less text CIs. These should transfer to unseen inferential error types such as altered p-values, SEs, CI bounds or test statistics. The remaining visible misses are count, percentage and N errors, which fall outside this principle, so I am not chasing them.

changes: Added a direction-consistency sub-check for sign flips in SE-only tables, which the earlier checks cannot see. It runs only where the text describes a table row variable unambiguously as positive or negative. "Unambiguous" means every sentence naming the variable gives the same polarity, with no negation and no other row variable in the sentence. The check then flags starred estimates for that variable whose sign contradicts the stated direction. It fires only when the row has a single starred estimate, or at least two-thirds of its starred estimates agree with the text.
